title: Usually employed workers struggle with job market shifts, AI impact
excerpt: Workers who are almost always employed are finding that seeking out a new role is a more daunting task.
content_html:
It used to be that if you're the type of person who always has a job, you're the type of person who can always find a job.

But a new analysis of job-finding rates complicates that picture. The study from the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond examines three types of workers and how they've fared in their job search.

"Primary workers," who make up about 55% of the US labor pool, are "almost always employed," per the analysis. They have steady work histories and usually only show up in unemployment statistics when something has gone wrong.

Historically, primary workers had the best odds of finding a new job. But their job-finding rates have fallen 13 percentage points from a November 2022 high to a September 2025 low — the biggest drop for any group the analysis covered.

Secondary workers, who make up about 14% of the labor pool, are often out of work or cycling through different jobs. They often make up the bulk of measured unemployment, and have a historically lower job-finding rate. While those workers still have a harder time finding jobs than their more attached peers, they haven't seen their fortunes fall as much; in the same period of November 2022 to September 2025, the job-finding rate for secondary workers fell just two percentage points.

This is new. In major recessions in the past, primary workers have seen their job-finding rates fall the most, followed by secondary workers. But now, primary workers are seeing that massive drop, while less secure secondary workers are not. So why would it be happening when the US economy is growing?

At the same time, the analysis finds that roles more exposed to AI — which the researchers define as the overlap of jobs' tasks with the capabilities listed in AI patents — have the biggest drop in job-finding rates. Before 2023, when ChatGPT became publicly accessible, job-finding rates for roles across levels of AI exposure moved together. Since then, outcomes have worsened dramatically for the AI-exposed fields.

AI has also shaken the hiring landscape for the new workers who might otherwise become strongly attached to the job market: As the report notes, research has found that generative AI can "substantially increase productivity at the task level (particularly for less-experienced workers), potentially altering the composition of new hiring."

For entry-level workers, that means a tighter labor market defined by roles requiring a wider variety of skills. For the experienced white-collar workers contending with a declining job-finding rate, that's meant taking drastic measures — including pay cuts.

It's not all bad news for white-collar workers. In the latest jobs report, both the professional and business services and information sectors added payrolls.

But those mild white-collar gains still weren't enough to offset a troubled labor market. On the whole, the US lost jobs in July — another sign that job hunting might not get much easier anytime soon.

content_html_zh:
过去，如果你是那种总是有工作的人，那么你就是那种总是能找到工作的人。

但对就业率的新分析使情况变得更加复杂。 里士满联邦储备银行的这项研究调查了三种类型的工人以及他们在求职中的表现。

根据分析，“初级工人”约占美国劳动力的 55%，“几乎总是有工作的”。 他们有稳定的工作经历，通常只有在出现问题时才会出现在失业统计数据中。

从历史上看，初级工人找到新工作的可能性最大。 但他们的求职率从 2022 年 11 月的高点下降到 2025 年 9 月的低点，下降了 13 个百分点，这是该分析涵盖的所有群体中降幅最大的。

二级工人约占劳动力资源的 14%，他们经常失业或从事不同的工作。 他们往往占统计失业率的大部分，而且就业率历来较低。 尽管这些工人比他们更依恋的同龄人仍然更难找到工作，但他们的财富并没有下降那么多； 2022年11月至2025年9月同期，二级工的就业率仅下降了两个百分点。

这是新的。 在过去的重大经济衰退中，初级工人的就业率下降幅度最大，其次是次级工人。 但现在，初级工人的收入大幅下降，而不太安全的二级工人则没有。 那么为什么在美国经济增长的时候会发生这种情况呢？

与此同时，分析发现，更多接触人工智能的角色——研究人员将其定义为工作任务与人工智能专利中列出的能力的重叠——的求职率下降幅度最大。 在 2023 年 ChatGPT 公开访问之前，不同人工智能暴露水平的职位的求职率会同步变化。 从那时起，人工智能领域的结果急剧恶化。

人工智能还动摇了新员工的招聘格局，否则他们可能会对就业市场产生强烈的依恋：正如报告指出的那样，研究发现生成式人工智能可以“大幅提高任务层面的生产力（特别是对于经验不足的员工），有可能改变新招聘的构成。”

对于初级工人来说，这意味着劳动力市场更加紧张，而这些角色需要更广泛的技能。 对于那些面临就业率下降的经验丰富的白领来说，这意味着采取严厉措施——包括减薪。

对于白领来说，这并不全是坏消息。 在最新的就业报告中，专业、商业服务和信息行业的就业人数均有所增加。

但白领人口的温和增长仍不足以抵消劳动力市场的困境。 总体而言，美国 7 月份失业了——这又一个迹象表明，短期内找工作可能不会变得容易得多。
